rv.q: Overall, it’s a good time for us “Dreamgirls” fans.
It is a jaw dropping production.
The result is a less than reverie-worthy “Dreamgirls.”

Christopher Betts' direction (massively alive during the group numbers, powerfully focused during more private scenes) and Amy Hall Garner's energetic choreography (wait until you see the "brass section" in concert) make this musical a true delight to watch.
Everyone does this Dreamgirls proud, really, and it begins with real affection for the history of R&B, still keenly felt in Tom Eyen ’s libretto and Henry Krieger ’s music.
Christopher D. Betts’ direction is explosive.

Paramount's Dreamgirls doesn't have that luster from the original production that debuted at the Imperial Theatre on December 20, 1981, City, where it received a standing ovation. However, it's still a solid performance audience will enjoy.
The cast that has been assembled by the Paramount director Christopher D. Betts and his staff is powerful with vocal ranges that are startling and amazing.

cn.t: Critics praise this "spectacular" production for its emotional power and sizzling performances, particularly the powerhouse lead turn as Effie, though the show delivers its familiar Supremes-inspired story with varying degrees of impact.
